headline: Andrew Coleman highlights Whitehaven Coal as a classic value opportunity during the green-transition panic, delivering better returns than Bitcoin or AI over five years.
reasoning: Coleman notes that as the green energy transition narrative dominated markets around 2021-2022, capital fled dirty industries so aggressively that Whitehaven Coal traded at under $1 per share, or roughly one times earnings. At that valuation, an investor was effectively guaranteed their money back within a year as long as the business remained solvent, with no one seriously expecting the energy transition to complete in under 12 months. Despite coal demand gradually declining since then, investors who bought at that trough have already made twice their money back in dividends alone, plus 10-14x in share price appreciation in under five years — outperforming Bitcoin and AI investments over the same period. Coleman uses this as a broader lesson that market panics create as much opportunity in unloved sectors as bubbles do in fashionable ones, and that value investors can profit by keeping a clear head while others are driven by sentiment.
quote: And the example I've picked up here for us to talk about is Whitehaven Coal. Now, for those who don't know, I presume most of our viewers probably do, but Whitehaven Coal is one of the largest thermal and coking coal producers in the world based here in Australia. And as that sort of joy of green energy. That idea that we were going to transition became more and more of a theme, and we saw lithium stocks and battery stocks and everyone else rise on the ASX. The corollary was that all the money poured out, flew away from the dirty companies. And who is more dirty than a coal miner? And as a result, you reached a point that in 2022, FY 22, between sort of June 2021 and June 2022, you could buy Whitehaven for less than a dollar a share, which worked out as roughly one times earnings. In other words, as long as Whitehaven didn't go bust in the next 365 days, you as an investor were guaranteed your money back... despite Whitehaven shrinking, in other words, the demand for coal slowly reducing over that time, you would have already made twice your money back in dividends alone, and another between 10 and 14 times, depending what you paid in share price growth in under five years. So that's a better return than investing in Bitcoin or AI or anyone else in that period, from owning the dirtiest of old world businesses.

quote: Whitehaven Coal (WHC) declined -27.5% in April. The driver of the decline was a weaker than expected March quarter production report.
